title: Liver functions
examples: What is the main job of the liver in the body?
How does the liver help clean our blood?
Can the liver make bile, and what is it used for?

explain.say: The liver performs many important jobs for your body.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the digestive system. Look at the oesophagus, the liver and the gall bladder. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
One job is deamination, which removes nitrogen from amino acids.
Detoxification is when the liver cleans harmful substances from your blood.
The liver also produces bile, which helps you digest fats in your gut.
In everyday life, when you eat a fatty meal, the bile helps break it down.
A common mistake is thinking the liver only stores energy for your body.

items: It does much more than just store energy.

faq.a: Deamination is the process where the liver removes the nitrogen group from amino acids. This waste nitrogen must then be converted into a safer form for removal.
asks: How does the liver get rid of nitrogen?
What happens to the nitrogen in amino acids?

faq.a: Detoxification is vital because it removes harmful chemicals and drugs from your bloodstream. This keeps your body functioning safely.
asks: Does the liver clean our blood?
What does the liver do with poisons?

faq.q: What is bile and where does it go?
faq.a: Bile is a greenish-yellow fluid produced by the liver. It travels through bile ducts into the small intestine to aid digestion.
asks: Where does the liver send bile?

faq.q: Can the liver fail if it has to do all these jobs?
faq.a: If the liver fails, it can build up toxins in the blood, which is very dangerous. This is why it must work correctly.
asks: What happens if the liver stops working?
Is the liver very important for survival?

faq.q: Are amino acids only used for building muscle?
faq.a: No, amino acids are essential building blocks, but the liver also processes them when they are in excess or need to be removed.
asks: Does the liver only deal with protein breakdown?
What is the fate of extra amino acids?

facts: The liver is a large organ located in the upper right side of the abdomen.
Deamination removes the nitrogen group from amino acids, forming ammonia.
The liver converts ammonia into urea, which is then excreted by the kidneys.
Bile contains bile salts, which help break down large fat globules.

quiz.say: The process of removing nitrogen from amino acids is called:
quiz.why: This is the specific biological term for removing the nitrogen group.

wrong.0: This is the process bile uses on fats, not the removal of nitrogen.
wrong.1: This is a broad term for all chemical reactions in the body.
wrong.3: This is a general term for cleaning the blood, not the specific chemical process.

quiz.say: What substance does the liver produce to help digest fats?
quiz.why: Bile salts are crucial for breaking down large fat molecules in the small intestine.

wrong.1: Urea is a waste product the liver helps to create, not the digestive aid.
wrong.2: Amino acids are the building blocks, not the substance for fat digestion.
wrong.3: Ammonia is a toxic waste product that the liver tries to remove.

quiz.say: If the liver fails to perform detoxification, what is a major risk?
quiz.why: The liver's primary role in detox is keeping blood clean of harmful substances.

wrong.1: While this is a problem, the immediate danger of failure is toxin buildup.
wrong.2: The liver does synthesize proteins, but toxin buildup is the more direct danger.
wrong.3: Kidneys filter waste, but the liver is responsible for detoxifying it first.
